A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of stereotype-driven implicit personalization. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original controlled-conversation experiments, demographic probing, response analyses and activation-steering results for three LLMs in Sections 3–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds random-label probe controls and MMLU/IFEval evaluations of steering.

M1.justification: The demographic probes and additive activation-steering procedure remain unchanged, including model-specific steering strengths and layers in Appendix D.4. V2's Equation (1) formalizes the operation already described in v1; the new control probes serve evaluation.

E1.justification: V2 adds MMLU knowledge-task and IFEval instruction-following evaluations, substantially extending coverage beyond demographic inference in synthetic conversations. The original conversation topics, demographic groups and three evaluated LLMs remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds structured random-label probes as comparators to true-label probes in Figure 2 and Appendix C.1. V1 displayed only true-label probe performance. The original model and steering comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces control-task evaluation with randomly assigned demographic-term labels and probe selectivity, plus five-shot MMLU accuracy and instance-level loose IFEval accuracy. These are substantive additional evaluation protocols. Existing conversation and steering settings are unchanged; specifying five-fold validation for the original probes does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Two substantive validation analyses are added: random-label controls examine probe reliability, and MMLU/IFEval tests examine steering's effects on general capabilities. V2 also adds illustrative stereotype-driven responses in Table 3. The earlier qualitative error analysis and steering-strength examples remain.

E5.justification: Section 3.3 now specifies five-fold cross-validation for estimating probe accuracy, whereas v1 stated only cross-validation. This clarifies statistical estimation without establishing additional runs. Existing 95% confidence-band and p < 0.01 significance-reporting conventions are retained.

E6.justification: V2 adds control-probe results, mitigation trajectories and MMLU/IFEval outcomes; Figure 7 reports significant decreases for OLMo on IFEval and Llama on MMLU. Existing numerical appendix tables retain their values. The unsteered example changes from male Elias in v1 Table 22 to female Amelia in v2 Table 23, matching Figure 1.

T1.justification: No new theoretical results, assumptions or proofs are introduced. Equation (1) restates the existing additive steering rule, while selectivity is adopted as a standard empirical probe diagnostic.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: stereotypes influence latent user demographics, can override explicit identities, and can be countered by steering toward the stated identity. The added suggestion of future user studies does not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses the tradeoff between experimental control and ecological validity and acknowledges omitted intersectional identities. It also interprets the new controls as supporting probe reliability and the capability tests as showing generally limited steering costs, with two significant-decrease exceptions.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the probe-validation fold count, explicitly identifies the conversations as English, and documents BBQ and model licenses. Code/data access, hardware, reported compute time and steering hyperparameters remain unchanged; moving the repository link into the main text does not change availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting probe controls, MMLU/IFEval, intersectional stereotypes, StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs. These modestly expand context without changing the central positioning against prior implicit-personalization work. Publication updates to existing references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits, expands the evaluation and limitations explanations, adds a displayed steering equation and revises acknowledgments. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 3 and Figures 6–7, and overlays random-label curves and legends on the four probe-accuracy figures. Existing appendix tables and the overall two-column layout are retained, with local reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added probe controls and capability tests strengthen validation, expanded limitations improve qualification, and Table 23 resolves the unsteered example's inconsistency with Figure 1. These gains are tempered by a new reporting error: Section 3.3 claims at least 75% selectivity, although its stated 100% true-probe accuracy and 30–44% control accuracy imply a difference of 56–70 percentage points.
